reason: Reproduced exactly, twice, at 1440x960 and 390x844. state=owner-editing opens on 'Send the invitations', data-date 2026-08-08, #b-edit-date value '8 August 2026'. Two presses of the -1 stepper: row data-date becomes 2026-08-06, .b-date reads 'Thu 6 Aug', .b-stepRead reads 'Thursday 6 August 2026 in 21 days', the grab's aria-label reads 'Thursday 6 August, in 21 days' - and #b-edit-date still reads '8 August 2026'. Same at 390 with +7: row 2026-08-15, readout 'in 30 days', field still '8 August 2026'. The code confirms why: setAway() in render-b.js carries the comment that it is 'the ONLY writer of an item's distance' and that every derived fact is written 'in the same frame, so the count, the date line, the accessible name and the readout cannot drift apart' - and it writes .b-away, .b-date, the grab label, .b-stepRead, the step disabled states and the ceiling note, but never the input that seeded itself from the same date. step()'s click handler does not write it either. The input is the one derived fact the single-writer contract leaves out, and it is the one control actually labelled 'When'. The second half is worse and also reproduced: focus #b-edit-date and press Enter without typing a character. commitDate() parses the stale '8 August 2026', gets away=23 against the item's current 21, calls setAway back to 2026-08-08, and only THEN hits 'if (to === from) return;' - which is now false, so it pushes a history entry. Measured result: the moment silently reverts, both stepper presses are gone, and the undo bar reads 'Send the invitations moved 2 days later.' (at 390: 'moved 7 days earlier.'). That sentence is true of the data and false about what the person did - the one reversibility surface in the product narrating an edit the owner never made, on the gesture the product calls its primary one. Not covered by the gates: interaction-check.mjs touches #b-edit-date only via fill()+Enter (typed date moves the moment, past-the-day refused, gone-day refused) and asserts the row, the readout and aria-invalid - never the input's own value after a stepper press, and never a bare Enter. Not taste, not a constraint breach: the fix is behavioural only, no palette, weight or architecture change.
sharpenedFix: Put the write inside setAway(), not in step()'s click handler - that is where the file's own single-writer comment says every derived fact is written, and it covers the stepper, the undo closures and any future nudge for free. After computing iso, do: var input = root.querySelector('#b-edit-date'); if (input && document.activeElement !== input) { input.value = F.fmt.medium(iso) + ' ' + F.fmt.year(iso); input.setAttribute('aria-invalid','false'); } - the focus guard is enough on its own, since a stepper press moves focus to the button, so it can never clobber a half-typed value. Verified in the page that F.fmt.medium(iso) + ' ' + F.fmt.year(iso) round-trips through F.parseDay exactly ('8 August 2026' -> 2026-08-08, '3 October 2026' -> 2026-10-03), so the field stays parseable by its own commit path. Then add the no-op guard at the top of commitDate, before setAway rather than after it: once iso is parsed and validated, if (iso === item.getAttribute('data-date')) { input.setAttribute('aria-invalid','false'); if (hint) hint.textContent = ''; return; }. Returning before setAway - not after, as the current 'to === from' line does - also spares the bare Enter a pointless place() relayout and the requestAnimationFrame keepInBand nudge. A confirm on an unchanged field must touch neither the model, the history nor the live region. Then assert both in interaction-check: after a stepper press the input's value must equal the readout's date, and a bare Enter on an untouched field must leave data-date and .b-undoText unchanged.
